amendment_history.note: الإصدار الأصلي (69 مادة موزعة على 12 فصلاً بلا تقسيم إلى أبواب) -- تصديقاً على نظام المجالس البلدية بموجب قرار مجلس الوزراء رقم (384) وتاريخ 24/9/1435هـ. يُلغي جزئياً المواد (2/ب، 2/ج، 7/ب، والفصل الثاني من الباب الثاني) من نظام البلديات والقرى الصادر بالمرسوم الملكي رقم (م/5) وتاريخ 21/2/1397هـ (م68)، مع استمرار المجالس البلدية القائمة وفق أحكامها المنظمة السابقة إلى حين تشكيل المجالس الجديدة (البند ثانياً من المرسوم). لا توجد أي تعديلات لاحقة مسجلة على هذا النظام حتى تاريخ هذا المسار (تم التحقق عبر ست لقطات أرشيفية من بوابة هيئة الخبراء تمتد من نوفمبر 2019 حتى ديسمبر 2025، جميعها بلا أي علم 'تعديلات المادة').

verification_methodology_note:
PRIMARY SOURCE ACCESS: laws.boe.gov.sa's live portal returned HTTP 503 Service Unavailable this pass for this law's exact detail URL (https://laws.boe.gov.sa/BoeLaws/Laws/LawDetails/9da91b16-62ba-41d8-b6f7-a9a700f21d07/1), consistent with this corpus's established pattern for this BOE portal. SIX independent Wayback Machine snapshots of this exact URL, spanning 22 Nov 2019 to 12 Dec 2025 (20191122184201, 20220625102159, 20230128014416, 20230529112910, 20240920083620, 20251212211934), were fetched via direct curl over the pre-configured proxy (WebFetch itself refused a direct web.archive.org fetch in this environment) and parsed offline with BeautifulSoup, not a naive regex/tag-stripping approach. All 69 'article_item' divs are present, in the same order, in every one of the six snapshots, and EVERY one of the 69 articles carries only the 'no_alternate' CSS class in every snapshot -- NONE carry a 'changed-article' class or any 'تعديلات المادة' amendment-changelog popup, in any snapshot. A full article-by-article byte-level diff (after whitespace normalization) between the earliest (22 Nov 2019) and latest (12 Dec 2025) snapshots -- a six-year span -- found ZERO textual differences across all 69 articles. This is the strongest form of stability evidence available via this method: this Law has undergone NO amendments since at least Nov 2019, and BOE's own page structure records none at any point in its own history. This law has 12 فصول (chapters) but NO أبواب (parts) -- confirmed by the complete absence of any 'باب' heading element anywhere in the archived HTML across all six snapshots; the chapter_structure field below reflects this flat 12-فصل structure. Article 1 alone carries an inline sub-heading in its own BOE-sourced H3 ('المادة الأولى: تعريفات:'); no other article has an inline title, so number_label_ar is used verbatim as sourced and no separate title_ar key is introduced for any article.

DECREE IDENTIFICATION: confirmed via THREE independent sources: (1) BOE's own metadata panel for this law ('أدوات إصدار النظام': 'مرسوم ملكي رقم (م/61) بتاريخ 4/10/1435'; 'تاريخ الإصدار': 1435/10/04هـ الموافق 31/07/2014م; 'تاريخ النشر': 1435/11/03هـ الموافق 29/08/2014م; 'الحالة': ساري); (2) the Ministry of Municipal, Rural Affairs and Housing's (MOMRAH, momah.gov.sa) OWN official website, which hosts two separately-dated official PDF copies of this exact Law's full text -- one uploaded Feb 2022 (momah.gov.sa/sites/default/files/2022-02/...) and one uploaded Oct 2025 (momah.gov.sa/sites/default/files/2025-10/...) -- both fetched live this pass and both opening with the same cover page ('نظام المجالس البلدية -- الصادر بالمرسوم الملكي رقم (م/61) وتاريخ 1435/10/04هـ') and, on page 2, an embedded scanned image of the original signed Royal Decree itself (read via direct visual inspection of the rendered page image at 200 DPI, not OCR/pdftotext -- pdftotext's default Arabic bidi handling produced reordered/ligature-broken text for this PDF's non-scanned pages, so PyMuPDF (fitz) get_text('text') was used instead for all machine-readable pages, which rendered correctly-ordered Arabic), showing 'الرقم: م/61' / 'التاريخ: 4/10/1435هـ', signed 'عبدالله بن عبدالعزيز آل سعود' (King Abdullah, who reigned until his death in Jan 2015 -- consistent with this decree's Jul/Aug 2014G date), and reciting the same Council of Ministers Resolution No. 384 dated 24/9/1435H; and (3) nezams.com, independently corroborating decree M/61, both dates, 'ساري' status, 69 articles, and the explicit statement 'لم يجرِ عليه تعديل' (no amendment has been made to it). MOMRAH is this law's own subject-matter regulator (Ministry of Municipal, Rural Affairs and Housing) and its website is a genuinely separate, independently-maintained primary source, not a re-hosted BOE mirror -- its PDF layout, styling, and hosting infrastructure are entirely distinct from BOE's. Per this corpus's four-tier verification taxonomy, two genuinely separate official/primary sources agreeing (BOE + MOMRAH) qualifies this track as TIER_1.

ARTICLE COUNT AND STRUCTURE: this corpus's own coverage_gap_map.json entry for this law explicitly flagged the article count as 'Not confirmed -- needs verification'. This pass resolves this: 69 articles, organized into 12 فصول (chapters), with NO أبواب (parts) -- independently confirmed by (a) BOE's own DOM structure (12 h3.الفصل headers interleaved with 69 article_item divs, in the exact sequence: فصل1=arts1-3, فصل2=arts4-11, فصل3=arts12-15, فصل4=arts16-25, فصل5=arts26-29, فصل6=arts30-36, فصل7=arts37-44, فصل8=arts45-50, فصل9=arts51-57, فصل10=arts58-61, فصل11=arts62-63, فصل12=arts64-69); (b) a full text extraction of both MOMRAH PDFs (2022 and 2025) via PyMuPDF, independently reproducing the identical 69-article/12-فصل sequence and identical chapter titles; and (c) nezams.com's own stated total of 69 articles. Every one of the 69 BOE article texts was diffed word-for-word (after whitespace normalization) against the corresponding MOMRAH PDF-extracted text; no substantive discrepancy was found (see known_unresolved_discrepancies for one confirmed, immaterial spelling anomaly common to BOTH sources).

ZERO AMENDMENTS -- POSITIVE STABILITY FINDING: unlike several other tracks in this corpus where BOE's main article text is found STALE relative to its own amendment changelog, this law shows the opposite, cleaner pattern: no amendment changelog exists at all, on any of the six Wayback snapshots spanning 2019-2025, and this is independently confirmed by nezams.com's explicit 'no amendment' statement and by the two independently-dated MOMRAH PDFs (2022, 2025) reproducing byte-for-byte-equivalent structure and content (modulo formatting/pagination differences from the PDF export process itself). All 69 articles are therefore ingested as legal_status_ar = اصلية (original), with empty history[] arrays.

REPEAL / PREDECESSOR: this law's own Article 68 (المادة الثامنة والستون), read directly from BOE's clean (non-OCR) HTML text and independently reproduced identically in both MOMRAH PDFs, states: 'يلغي هذا النظام المواد (2/ب، 2/ج، 7/ب، والفصل الثاني من الباب الثاني) من نظام البلديات والقرى، الصادر بالمرسوم الملكي ذي الرقم (م/5) والتاريخ 21/2/1397هـ، ويلغي كل ما يتعارض معه من أحكام.' -- i.e. it EXPRESSLY, but only PARTIALLY, repeals four specifically-named provisions (Articles 2(b), 2(c), 7(b), and Chapter Two of Part Two) of the Law of Municipalities and Villages (نظام البلديات والقرى, Royal Decree M/5, 21/2/1397H, roughly 1977G) -- NOT a full supersession of that law, which otherwise remains in force for everything else it covers. That predecessor law is NOT already ingested in this corpus (confirmed via a repository-wide search for 'البلديات والقرى' prior to this pass) and is NOT independently fetched, verified, or ingested by this track, consistent with this corpus's one-law-per-pass practice and the instruction to model a repeal relationship ONLY when explicitly named in the ingested law's own text (which it is here, precisely and narrowly, per Article 68) -- see known_unresolved_discrepancies, key municipal_councils_predecessor_m5_1397h_partial_repeal_confirmed_primary. Distinct from this corpus's ALREADY-INGESTED regions_law track (provincial/regional administration, a wholly separate subject matter and separate Royal Decree) and from the ALREADY-INGESTED municipal_realestate_law/municipal_realestate_implementing_regulation tracks (real-estate zoning classification for municipalities, also a wholly separate subject matter) -- no overlap or conflict with either was found.

IMPLEMENTING REGULATIONS -- NOT INGESTED THIS PASS: this law's own text references several companion regulations to be issued by the Minister or Council of Ministers: اللائحة التنفيذية للنظام (general implementing regulation, Article 66), لائحة انتخاب أعضاء المجالس البلدية (election regulation, referenced throughout Chapter 4/5), لائحة الحملات الانتخابية (campaign regulation, Article 23), and اللائحة المالية (financial regulation, Article 67). A WebSearch this pass located momah.gov.sa/ar/node/13105 ('اللائحة التنفيذية لنظام المجالس البلدية'), confirming at least the general implementing regulation has in fact been issued and is hosted on MOMRAH's own site. Per this corpus's one-law-per-pass practice and this track's task brief, NONE of these regulations are fetched, verified, or ingested this pass -- flagged as a candidate for a dedicated follow-up ingestion pass (see known_unresolved_discrepancies, key municipal_councils_implementing_regs_not_ingested).

No legal text is altered beyond whitespace/line-break normalization needed to render BOE's HTML as plain text, and removal of decorative Arabic tatweel/kashida characters (U+0640) that appeared mid-word in a handful of BOE's own rendered spans (e.g. 'ريـال', 'الصـادر', 'بالمـرسـوم') -- a typographic justification artifact with no semantic content of its own, consistent with this corpus's established text-cleanliness convention (verified: removing it changes no word's spelling or meaning). Arabic governs; no translation/paraphrase/interpretation performed on the Arabic text (English descriptions in this note and in document_en/issuing_authority_en are for indexing only). Read-only over input; deterministic over outputs.

known_unresolved_discrepancies.description: The heading for Chapter (فصل) 10 reads, verbatim, in BOTH independently-fetched primary sources (BOE's own HTML across all six Wayback snapshots, and BOTH MOMRAH-hosted PDFs from 2022 and 2025): 'الفصل العاشر: مخلفات أعضاء المجالس البلدية' -- using 'مخلفات' (literally 'remnants/leftovers/residues') rather than the substantively-expected 'مخالفات' (violations/offences), which is the word actually used inside this chapter's own articles (58-61, covering the violations committee, procedure, and penalties for council members) and is the word used for the parallel, differently-numbered Chapter 9 ('الفصل التاسع: المخالفات الانتخابية' -- Electoral Violations). Because this exact spelling is reproduced identically across BOE (six independent snapshots spanning 2019-2025) and two separately-uploaded MOMRAH PDFs (2022 and 2025), this is very likely a genuine typographical error in the Law's own original gazetted text (or a persistent, uncorrected error carried into BOE's own digitisation) rather than a scraping or transcription artifact introduced by this pass. Per this corpus's trust policy, this track does NOT silently 'correct' the heading to what a reader might expect -- it reproduces 'مخلفات أعضاء المجالس البلدية' verbatim in chapter_structure's title_ar field for Chapter 10, exactly as it appears in both independently-fetched primary sources, and flags the anomaly here for transparency.

This law's own Article 68 (المادة الثامنة والستون), read directly from BOE's clean HTML text and independently reproduced identically in both MOMRAH PDFs, states: 'يلغي هذا النظام المواد (2/ب، 2/ج، 7/ب، والفصل الثاني من الباب الثاني) من نظام البلديات والقرى، الصادر بالمرسوم الملكي ذي الرقم (م/5) والتاريخ 21/2/1397هـ، ويلغي كل ما يتعارض معه من أحكام.' -- i.e. it explicitly, but only PARTIALLY, repeals four specifically-named provisions of the Law of Municipalities and Villages (نظام البلديات والقرى, Royal Decree M/5, 21/2/1397H) -- Articles 2(b), 2(c), 7(b), and Chapter Two of Part Two of that law -- NOT a full supersession; the Law of Municipalities and Villages otherwise remains the governing statute for municipalities/villages generally and is not affected beyond these four named provisions. That predecessor law is NOT currently ingested anywhere in this corpus (confirmed via a repository-wide search for 'البلديات والقرى' prior to this pass finding no existing track) and its own text was NOT independently fetched, verified, or ingested by this track -- noted here as confirmed historical/cross-reference context only, consistent with this corpus's standard practice for confirmed partial-repeal relationships and its one-law-per-pass rule. A dedicated future pass ingesting نظام البلديات والقرى (M/5, 1397H) in its own right is a candidate follow-up, distinct from and not to be confused with this corpus's ALREADY-INGESTED regions_law track (a wholly separate, later statute on provincial/regional administration) or its ALREADY-INGESTED municipal_realestate_law/municipal_realestate_implementing_regulation tracks (real -estate zoning classification for municipalities, also a wholly separate subject).

Unlike several other tracks in this corpus where BOE's live article body is found materially stale relative to its own amendment changelog, this law shows the cleaner, opposite pattern: NO article, across any of six independently-fetched BOE-via-Wayback-Machine snapshots spanning 22 Nov 2019 to 12 Dec 2025, ever carries a 'changed-article' CSS class or any 'تعديلات المادة' amendment-changelog popup, and a full word-for-word diff (after whitespace normalization) of all 69 articles between the earliest and latest snapshots -- a six-year span -- found ZERO textual differences. This is independently corroborated by nezams.com's explicit statement 'لم يجرِ عليه تعديل' (no amendment has been made to it) and by two independently-uploaded official MOMRAH PDFs (Feb 2022 and Oct 2025) reproducing the identical 69-article/12-فصل structure and content. This track therefore records ALL 69 articles as legal_status_ar = اصلية (original) with empty history[] arrays, and amendment_history below contains only the single original-issuance entry (Royal Decree M/61 itself). This finding is flagged here per this corpus's trust policy of documenting verification findings explicitly rather than silently assuming stability without recording how it was established.

This law has 12 فصول (chapters) but NO أبواب (parts/parts-level grouping above chapters) -- confirmed by the complete absence of any 'باب' heading element anywhere in BOE's archived HTML across all six independently-fetched snapshots, and by the complete absence of any باب-level heading in either MOMRAH PDF. The sole reference to 'باب' anywhere in this law's own text is inside Article 68's repeal clause, which names 'الفصل الثاني من الباب الثاني' (Chapter Two of Part Two) as part of the STRUCTURE OF THE PREDECESSOR LAW (نظام البلديات والقرى) being partially repealed -- NOT a أبواب grouping within this law itself. This track's chapter_structure field reflects a flat, single-level list of 12 فصول entries (no nested 'sections' key), consistent with this corpus's nazaha_law precedent for a flat single-level chapter_structure (there using أبواب as the flat unit; here using فصول, since فصل is the terminology this law's own source text actually uses for its 12 top-level groupings, and no أبواب level exists above them).

This law's own articles reference several companion regulations to be issued by the Minister or Council of Ministers: اللائحة التنفيذية للنظام (general implementing regulation -- referenced in Article 1's definitions and Article 66); لائحة انتخاب أعضاء المجالس البلدية (election regulation -- referenced throughout Chapters 3-5, e.g. Articles 16, 17, 20, 21); لائحة الحملات الانتخابية (campaign regulation -- Article 23); and اللائحة المالية (financial regulation, issued by Council of Ministers decision on the Minister's proposal -- Article 67). A WebSearch this pass located momah.gov.sa/ar/node/13105 ('اللائحة التنفيذية لنظام المجالس البلدية'), confirming at least the general implementing regulation has in fact been issued and is hosted on MOMRAH's own official site; a further search hit (qanoniah.com) referenced 'اللائحة التنفيذية لعمل المجالس البلدية' as well. Per this corpus's established one-law-per-pass precedent, NONE of these regulations are fetched, verified, or ingested this pass -- flagged here as a candidate for a dedicated follow-up ingestion pass.
